items.summary: In Bihar’s Bhagalpur district, a 2,400 MW thermal power plant is rising on land whose true costs are only beginning to surface. Awarded to Adani Power Ltd in a Rs 30,000 crore deal, the Pirpainti project has moved forward through disputed compensation, broken promises, and a public hearing farmers say was engineered to silence them. The two-part series traces what has been erased in the process. The first part examines how hundreds of farmers across 12 villages have watched their orchards vanish without adequate compensation for either land or their orchards. The second turns to a community left out of the process entirely: two Santhal and Pahariya Adivasi hamlets sitting within the project site itself, absent from official lists of affected communities — left with no guaranteed right to compensation or rehabilitation. Adani Power rejected any suggestion of legal or regulatory violations, saying the Pirpainti project is fully compliant and that it supports local communities and jobs. *** On the morning of February 19, Sushil Kumar walked out of a meeting with government officials believing his land and trees would remain safe for 15 days. The 49-year-old was among a group of farmers in Bihar’s Bhagalpur who had gathered for a high-level meeting, attended by officials of district administration, the police and the state’s Energy Department. They wanted permission from the farmers to cut 100 trees to build a road to a 2400 MW thermal power plant being built by Adani Power. The meeting went on from 11:30 am to 12:45 pm at the end of which a clear agreement was reached: no work would take place on the disputed land for the next 15 days. The farmers, who had to rush for another hearing, for which they were served notices on the same morning, left with some relief. The notices were served under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which permits an executive magistrate to take preventive action to maintain public order. It wanted them to appear before the official and furnish a bond of Rs 1 lakh each. items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently denied anticipatory bail to a lawyer accused of molesting a woman and assaulting and disrobing her husband and her son [ Vikas Yadav v. State of NCT of Delhi and Anr ]. Justice Girish Kathpalia observed, “Grant of anticipatory bail in such circumstances would convey wrong signals to the society at large that being a practicing advocate can be a license to indulge in such brazen lawlessness and would erode the public confidence in the rule of law.” Justice Girish Kathpalia The incident took place in January following a dispute over gym being operated in the basement of the complainant’s house. The complainant, Rita Garg, stated that she was assaulted and molested by the lawyer, Vikas Yadav, and other accused persons. She claims that they assaulted her husband, who suffered a fracture as result, as well as her son, who was beaten, disrobed and left naked on a road. The entire incident was captured on CCTV. Yadav was declared a proclaimed offender by the magistrate. He moved the High Court Court seeking anticipatory bail. The prosecution told the Court that Yadav was absconding and did not join investigation despite issuance of non-bailable warrants and declaration as a proclaimed offender. The Court agreed with the submissions made on Yadav’s behalf that proclaimed offenders can seek anticipatory bail, however, only under exceptional circumstances. It went on to note Yadav’s conduct in assaulting persons with a heavy gym rod and the disrobing of the complainant's son. It stated that the psychological injury inflicted by Yadav in disrobing the man was more serious than inflicting physical injuries. Terming Yadav’s conduct as “shocking and barbaric”, the Court rejected the argument that his profession of being an advocate is a circumstance favouring grant of anticipatory bail. “Of course, all advocates, being officers of the court, deserve respect. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Justice Sanjay Sharma The PIL, filed by Telecom Watchdog, has challenged BSNL’s decision to allow bids from companies which use equipment supplied by Lavelle Networks. As per the plea, use of Lavelle's equipment would make a company ineligible to participate in the bid because of its links with Bharti Airtel, a telecom service provider. It is the petitioner's case that the project aims to digitise nearly 27,000 post offices to support postal, banking and insurance services. The petition argues that the project’s eligibility conditions barred telecom service providers, like Airtel, and their group companies from participating. It alleges that BSNL failed to enforce these conditions by allowing two bidders, Sify Technologies and Pace Digitek, to quote equipment supplied by Lavelle without the required self-certificates. "In this tender, there were four bidders. All the bidders including their respective OEMs submitted their self-certificates, barring Lavelle. BSNL should have rejected the bids of Respondent Nos.3 (Sify Technologies Ltd) & 4 (Pace Digitek Ltd), which had quoted Lavelle’s equipment without self-certificate. This omission by BSNL is deliberate attempt to favour the bidder for letting them bypass the risk of submitting a false certificate," states the petition. The dispute over Lavelle’s eligibility centres on its relationship with Airtel. According to the petition, Airtel disclosed that it acquired a stake in Lavelle, a Bengaluru-based networking technology company, in 2022 and increased it to 45.6 percent in 2023. The petition claims that Airtel exercises significant influence over Lavelle. It contends that their relationship brings the company within the tender restrictions. BSNL, however, rejected the complaint in September, maintaining that Airtel’s interest did not amount to control over Lavelle’s board, management or policy decisions that would make the two companies a parent-subsidiary or group company under the tender conditions. items.title: Kerala High Court to wait for police report before deciding on action against judge whose son killed scooterist
items.summary: The family of the 55-year-old man, who died recently after a Mercedez-Benz car driven by the minor son of an additional sessions judge hit his scooter, has submitted a complaint before the Kerala High Court Chief Justice seeking an enquiry into the judicial officer's conduct. The judicial officer, who is serving as a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal judge in Iranjalakuda, has already been arraigned as an accused by the police under Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act since he is the registered owner of the car which caused the accident. Sources told Bar & Bench that the High Court's Administrative Committee held a preliminary meeting on October 27 to examine the material concerning the accident. Since the police investigation is still underway, the committee decided not to take any action against the judicial officer at present and await further material from the investigation agency. The committee comprises Chief Justice Soumen Sen and five of the senior-most judges of the High Court. The complaint submitted by the victim's children requests the Chief Justice to examine whether an administrative or disciplinary enquiry is warranted against the judicial officer. They have requested the Chief Justice to seek reports from the competent authority with regard to the registration and progress of the criminal case, particularly on the invocation of Section 199A of the MV Act. Section 199A provides that when a minor commits a motor vehicle offence, the guardian or vehicle owner is presumed to be responsible and can be prosecuted and punished, subject to statutory exceptions. They have further sought measures to safeguard the independence and impartiality of the investigation, the preservation of relevant CCTV footage from Cheranalloor Police Station and an objective examination of the allegations against the judicial officer. The family of the victim was informed that their complaint has been placed before the appropriate administrative authority. According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered by the Cheranalloor police, the victim identified as Jayabalakrishnan (55), was returning home after closing his roadside eatery when the accident occurred around 2:20 AM on Sunday morning. The car driven by the 17-year-old boy was travelling from Vallarpadam towards Kalamassery when it allegedly hit the scooter near a Ford showroom on Container Road. items.title: SAT imposes ₹1 lakh costs on MCX, quashes ₹1.5 crore penalty on Ventura Securities
items.summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) has imposed ₹1 lakh in costs on the Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) for levying a ₹1.49 crore penalty on Ventura Securities Limited despite the maximum permissible penalty under a Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) circular being ₹2 lakh. [VSL Vs MCX] The tribunal also set aside the penalty order and directed MCX to immediately refund ₹1.76 crore, inclusive of GST, debited from Ventura's account. A Bench of Justice PS Dinesh Kumar (Presiding Officer), Meera Swarup (Technical Member) and Dr Dheeraj Bhatnagar (Technical Member) held that such conduct by an exchange functioning as a first-line regulator could not be countenanced. " Such act on the part of the respondent exchange, which is a first line regulator cannot be countenanced, " the SAT said. The dispute arose from an order dated September 28, 2026, passed by MCX's Member Committee imposing a penalty of ₹1.49 crore on Ventura Securities for allegedly violating client-level open position limits. According to Ventura, the allegation was that one of its clients had exceeded the permissible 2 percent open position limit in natural gas options, with the position allegedly reaching 27 percent. Ventura challenged the penalty before SAT, questioning both the legality of the order and the quantum of the penalty imposed. During the proceedings, Ventura pointed out that SV Krishnamohan, an independent external expert whose signature appeared on the penalty order, had ceased to be a member of the committee on March 20, 2026. However, the penalty order was issued more than six months later, on September 28. MCX acknowledged the discrepancy and submitted that the inclusion of Krishnamohan's signature was a bona fide error. It requested that the matter be remitted for reconsideration. Ventura further argued that MCX had failed to issue any alert concerning the alleged breach of position limits. It also submitted that even assuming the violation was established, a SEBI circular dated September 9, 2026, prescribed a maximum penalty of ₹2 lakh. MCX did not dispute these submissions. The tribunal noted that MCX had already debited ₹1.76 crore, comprising the penalty and applicable GST, from Ventura's account on October 14. It held that the penalty order was legally unsustainable and directed an immediate refund. MCX subsequently requested the tribunal to refrain from imposing costs. However, the Bench rejected the request. Advocates Rushin Kapadia, Sumit Agrawal

items.title: Counting backwards: The prior-price rule and the regulation of discount claims in Indian e-commerce
items.summary: A discount is a comparison and a comparison is only as reliable as its reference point. A struck-through figure beside a lower price represents that the lower price is a genuine concession. Indian law has so far policed that representation only after the event, through the general prohibition on misleading advertisements. The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 , notified on September 9, 2026 and in force from January 1, 2027, add a direct rule. Rule 4(13) requires an e-commerce entity or seller that announces a price reduction to disclose a “prior price” alongside the reduced price. This article argues that Rule 4(13) rests on a sound benchmark but leaves four questions open: what period the benchmark covers, how prominently it must be shown, who bears the duty on a marketplace and how a claim can be tested. It reads the rule against the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Court of Justice of the European Union’s decision in Aldi Süd , which interprets a provision with the same 30-day benchmark. The Rule in its statutory setting Rule 4(13) reads in full: “(13) Where an e-commerce entity or the seller announces a price reduction for any goods or services on its platform, it shall indicate the prior price of such goods or services along with reduced price. Explanation – For the purposes of this sub-rule, “prior price” means the lowest price of a good or service thirty days prior to the announcement of price reduction.” The sub-rule was made under Section 101(2)(zg) of the Act , in the same notification as Rule 4(12), which requires sponsored listings to carry “clear and prominent disclosures”. Under Rule 8 of the 2020 Rules , a contravention attracts the provisions of the Act; the Rules create no separate penalty. First, Rule 4(13) names both the “e-commerce entity” and “the seller”, although Rule 3(1)(b) of the 2020 Rules defines an e-commerce entity so as to exclude a seller on a marketplace. Second, it requires the prior price to be “indicate[d]”, without the prominence that Rule 4(12) requires. Why the Rule exists Existing law gave consumers a ceiling but not a history. Rule 18(2) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 bars a sale above the price declared on the package, as the Department of Consumer Affairs has told Parliament . items.title: Sameer Chugh appointed General Counsel of Diageo India
items.summary: Beverage major Diageo India has appointed corporate lawyer Sameer Chugh as its new General Counsel, effective December 1, 2026. Chugh succeeds Shobhana Nikam, who has decided to step down for personal reasons, effective October 31, 2026, following a four-year tenure. Bengaluru-based Chugh will report directly to Praveen Someshwar, CEO & President, India with a dotted line reporting to Global General Counsel Randall Ingber. He will also join the India Executive Committee and the Global Legal Leadership Team. Chugh brings over 30 years of legal expertise across industries, spanning corporate governance, M&A, litigation and regulatory affairs. He joins Diageo from Games24x7, where he served as Chief Legal Officer and General Counsel. Previously, he was the Group General Counsel at Bharti Group, overseeing legal strategy across multiple businesses and jurisdictions. His career also includes senior leadership roles at British Telecom, Essar Group, and Cummins, alongside private practice at leading law firms.

items.summary: A Bengaluru commercial court recently set aside an arbitral award directing the Karnataka Department of State Education Research and Training (DSERT) to pay over ₹9 crore to Puthur Infotech in a dispute concerning maintenance services provided to 4,396 schools across the State. [DESERT v. Puthur Info] Judge Vijaya Kumar Rai held that the arbitrator had committed patent illegality by failing to consider the State government's objection that the company's claims were barred by limitation. " The omission to record a finding on limitation is a fundamental defect which goes to the root of the matter and renders the award patently illegal for non-consideration of the defence raised by the respondent ," the Court observed. The dispute arose from a 2013 tender issued by DSERT for maintenance of UPS systems, printers and LCD projectors in 1,763 government high schools and 2,633 aided high schools across Karnataka. Puthur Infotech secured the ₹7.19 crore contract for the period between April 2014 and April 2015. While the government paid ₹5.07 crore, the company alleged that outstanding payments had not been released despite satisfactory completion of its contractual obligations. The company subsequently approached the MSME Council, which referred the dispute to arbitration after conciliation failed. In May 2023, the sole arbitrator, former Himachal Pradesh High Court Chief Justice L Narayana Swamy, awarded the company ₹7.75 crore, including interest, besides another ₹1.27 crore with interest. The arbitrator also rejected the government's counterclaim seeking ₹4.34 crore for alleged deficiencies in services. Challenging the award, the State argued that 16 of the 17 invoices underlying the company's claim were time-barred when proceedings were initiated in 2018. The commercial court agreed, noting that payments under these invoices had become due more than three years before the company approached the MSME Council. It rejected the company's contention that repeated assurances from government authorities extended the limitation period. The Court further held that the arbitrator had wrongly rejected the government's counterclaim merely because it had not first approached the MSME Council. It clarified that buyers were not required to initiate independent proceedings before the Council to maintain counterclaims in arbitration. items.title: Delhi High Court slams State for failure to implement open prisons; warns Chief Secretary of contempt
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday warned the State's Chief Secretary of contempt of court for the government’s failure to implement directions issued by the Supreme Court in February this year to expand and strengthen Open Correctional Institutions (OCIs) or open prisons. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma orally remarked that it will call Delhi's top civil servant to the High Court and frame contempt of court charges if he cannot give a satisfactory response. The stern warning came from the Court after it noted that despite the top court’s direction in February 2026 and subsequent orders of the High Court, the government and prison authorities failed to act and the matter had “not moved an inch”. It added that government officials, tasked with reporting compliance with the top court’s order, had shown a completely callous approach. The Bench noted that the Supreme Court had asked the government authorities not to send officers below the rank of secretary to the meeting of the monitoring committee. Despite clear directions, a deputy secretary-rank officer, whom the ACJ referred to as a “joker”, was sent to the meeting. “You sent your joker in the committee meeting. You want to show us the minutes of the meeting? We don’t want to wash dirty linen in our order about what the state has done,” the Court said. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Justice Sanjay Sharma Notably, the Court today issued a contempt of court notice to the Director General (DG) Prisons. It said that the officer had shown “disregard” to the High Court and Supreme Court since, despite a clear order directing him to look into the matter, he made his subordinate swear an affidavit with incomplete information. However, the Court said it was deferring its order to draw contempt against other officers since the Special Secretary (Home) joined the proceeding and gave an assurance that a detailed response with para-wise compliance with the Supreme Court order will be produced before the Court. “Mr Lao [Sanjay Lao, Standing Counsel (Criminal) for Delhi] assures that the meeting of the monitoring committee will be attended by highest officials of the prison department and the state government,” the Court recorded in its order. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently refused to quash criminal cases filed by two neighbouring families against each other after a dispute about garbage disposal in their Bengaluru apartment complex escalated into physical violence [ Chandrashekhar Gupta v. State of Karnataka ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj , on October 5, dismissed the petitions filed to quash the cases by Chandrashekhar Gupta and his wife, Neha Gupta, and their neighbours, Anant Gopal and his wife Swathi Sharma. The judge also emphasised that disagreements between neighbours must not escalate into physical violence. " The familiar exhortation, ‘Love thy neighbour’, embodies a principle of practical importance for peaceful coexistence ... The resort to physical violence is never an acceptable means of resolving a neighbourhood dispute ,” the Court said. items.title: Allahabad High Court moots disciplinary action after lawyers vandalise courtroom, raise slogans
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday said it will recommend disciplinary and contempt of court proceedings against lawyers who interrupted its proceedings by raising slogans in the court corridors [Devendra Kumar v State of UP] The order was passed by Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal who happened to hear the sloganeering and ruckus. The lawyers were protesting against the alleged ill-treatment of a lawyer by another judge, Justice Ajay Bhanot . During the protest, the lawyers allegedly broke furniture and other items inside courtroom number 49 where Justice Bhanot was holding court. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal heard the sloganeering while he was hearing a bail matter. Justice Deshwal was informed that lawyers present in the corridor were protesting against the ill-treatment of a lawyer. Justice Deshwal then observed that the lawyers were interrupting the court proceedings. "Such incident amounts to interference in the Court proceedings as poor litigants come to the High Court for redressal of their grievance, and merely because some of the Advocates have problem with particular Court, they cannot be permitted to raise slogans, shout and disturb to other Courts' proceedings and use such words which is in the nature to intimidate the Court. This is wholly unjustified," the bench said Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal The Court added that the conduct of the lawyers was absolutely contemptuous. It directed the Registrar (Protocol) to check the CCTV footage of the particular area outside its courtroom and identify the advocates involved in sloganeering. "After identifying the Advocates, the matter may be referred to the Bar Council of U.P. for initiation of disciplinary proceedings as well as initiating the contempt proceedings against them," Justice Deshwal ordered. The matter will be heard next on November 19. [Read Order]

items.title: Government Law College, Dharmapuri wins SRM School of Law's 8th National Level Tamil Moot Court Competition
items.summary: A team from Government Law College, Dharmapuri has won the 8th National Level Tamil Moot Court Competition 2026 hosted by SRM School of Law, SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), Kattankulathur. The team comprised Malavika M , Jayanthi A and Divyaprabha CK. Mother Teresa Law College secured the runner-up position. The Best Memorial and Best Researcher awards went to participants from Government Law College, Karaikudi, while the Best Speaker award was presented to a participant from Government Law College, Tirunelveli. The competition brought together 42 teams and 126 participants from law institutions across India. The final round was adjudicated Justice (Retd) Prabha Sridevan , former Judge of the Madras High Court; Prof (Dr) N Kayalvizhi , Principal, Dr Ambedkar Government Law College, Pattaraiperumbudur; Prof (Dr) Jaya Gowri , Principal, Dr Ambedkar Government Law College, Pudupakkam; Senior Advocate Geetha of the Madras High Court; and Senior Advocate GV Shobha of the Madras High Court. The competition was conducted across three stages. During the preliminary rounds, 42 judges evaluated teams on their interpretation and application of law, use of legal authorities, quality of legal reasoning and ability to respond to questions from the Bench. Eight teams advanced to the quarterfinals, where they competed in a knockout format. Addressing the participants, Justice (Retd) Bhavani Subbarayan emphasised the importance of strengthening research, drafting, pleading and analytical skills. She highlighted the value of practical exposure and the need for an unwavering commitment to justice. Justice N Mala of the Madras High Court encouraged students to embrace both success and failure as integral parts of their professional journeys, describing failure as a steppingstone to success. Drawing on her experience as a first-generation lawyer, she spoke about overcoming self-doubt, persevering through challenges and building professional confidence through experience. She urged students to uphold integrity, embrace continuous learning and build their careers on a strong ethical foundation.

items.title: Dropping the issue since they have apologised: Lawyer who sent notice to Congress for tweet about CJI
items.summary: Supreme Court lawyer Meenesh Dubey will not be filing a criminal contempt of court case against the Kerala unit of the Congress party for their social media post against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. This development comes in light of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) tendering an unconditional apology to CJI Kant over a tweet effectively calling for his resignation. The apology was submitted by KPCC President Sunny Joseph in a formal reply dated October 22 to a legal notice issued by Dubey, who is also the joint secretary of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA). When asked whether he would be filing a contempt of court petition, Dubey replied in the negative. "Since they have apologised, I will not be pursuing the matter further," Dubey told Bar & Bench . Dubey had earlier threatened to initiate criminal contempt of court proceedings after a post appeared on October 12 from the official X handle (@INCKerala) stating: "Dear Surya Kant, If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it." In his reply, KPCC clarified that the post was drafted and published by party worker Vijay Thottathil without the leadership's knowledge, consent, or consultation. Joseph confirmed that Thottathil had been immediately stripped of his responsibilities and was instructed to issue a public apology. The party also undertook to publish its official clarification and apology on its public social media channels.

items.title: Kerala High Court seeks State's response on plea against GO exempting Vigilance Bureau from RTI; no stay
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the State government on public interest litigation (PIL) petitions challenging its recent decision to exempt certain sections of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) from disclosure under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 [ Adv PK Muralikrishnan v. State of Kerala & Ors. ] A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM also asked the State government to clarify whether the decision to exempt T1 and T2 sections of the VACB from the purview of the RTI Act includes information regarding vigilance inquiries against officials. However, the Court did not impose a stay on the government decision. Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM (Kerala HC) The decision to exempt T1 and T2 sections was notified by the Kerala government through a Government Order (GO) published in the Kerala Gazette on October 22, 2026. The GO was issued invoking Section 24(4) of the RTI Act, which allows state governments to exempt specified intelligence and security organisations from the Act, subject to conditions laid down in the provision. At least two PILs were filed before the Kerala High Court challenging this move. One of the PILs was moved by advocate PK Muralikrishnan who was a Legal Advisor to the VACB in Kerala. Another was moved by Joy Kaitharath who is a prominent anti-corruption and RTI activist. The petitioners argued that the GO in question discloses no functions, reasons, or objective material forming the basis of the opinion that "T1" and "T2" Sections constitute "intelligence and security organisations". They submitted that the mandate of these Sections essentially relates to processing complaints and investigations of corruption against public servants. " Their exclusion from the RTI framework, therefore, has significant implications for public access to information concerning the functioning of the anti-corruption machinery ", Kaitharath argued in his PIL. items.title: Delhi High Court slams tax officer for ₹3.91 crore IT demand against security guard with EWS certificate
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently quashed a ₹3.91 crore income tax demand against a security guard and cook, strongly criticising the Assessing Officer (AO) for failing to apply his mind in the case [Lalit Vs Union of India] A division bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Aditi Choudhary found that the officer had arbitrarily attributed transactions worth nearly ₹50 crore to the petitioner without looking into his claim that his Permanent Account Number (PAN) had been misused. The Court was particularly critical of the officer's failure to understand the nature of the transactions. " This approach of the AO reveals that he has not even cared to understand the nature of transaction –either he did not understand the basics of accounting or he did not want to," the bench said. Justice Dinesh Mehta and Justice Aditi Choudhary The petitioner, Lalit, worked as a contractual security guard and cook at Ashoka Hotel and Vigyan Bhawan in Delhi between 2015 and 2019. He claimed to have obtained a PAN card merely as government-issued identity proof despite having no taxable income. In February 2024, he received a notice alleging cash transactions involving Montage Enterprises Private Limited, a packaging materials company. The notice referred to cash payments of ₹24.86 crore and cash sales of ₹24.62 crore against his PAN. Lalit denied undertaking these transactions and filed complaints with the police and cyber cell, alleging identity theft. However, the AO treated both transactions as his turnover of ₹49.48 crore and assessed 8% as taxable income, resulting in a demand of approximately ₹3.91 crore. The Court found that the officer had effectively counted the same transaction twice by adding the gross amount and the net amount remaining after tax collection. It also noted that no independent inquiry had been conducted to establish Lalit's connection with Montage Enterprises. The Court observed that Lalit had produced bank statements and explained that he had withdrawn provident fund money to meet financial needs. He had also obtained an Economically Weaker Section (EWS) certificate and sought a school fee waiver for his children. The bench said these circumstances warranted empathy and objective scrutiny. It rejected the Income Tax Department's argument that Lalit should pursue the statutory appellate remedy. items.title: Delhi SIR: Why is ECI forcing excluded voters to submit Form 6 as first-time voters? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked the Election Commission of India (ECI) why voters enrolled in earlier voter lists but left out from the draft of the revised voter list being prepared as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi, are being compelled to submit Form 6 meant to for the registration of first-time voters. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea alleging lack of transparency in notices issued to voters by election authorities in Delhi during SIR. “ Form 6 is for someone seeking enrolment for the first time. Form 8 is for the correction or shifting of residence. Suppose a person was enrolled in Vasant Kunj and has now shifted to Sarita Vihar. That person can disclose the earlier polling booth, electoral roll particulars and voter number, and provide the new address. Why should that person be required to submit Form 6?” CJI Kant asked the ECI today. Justice Bagchi also agreed that issuing Form 6 to a person already enrolled in an earlier voter list may be an erroneous approach. “Why should someone who was already enrolled in the electoral roll be required to submit Form 6? Form 6 is meant for someone seeking enrolment for the first time,” the Bench added. Justice Bagchi went on to observe that the right to vote is a crucial right that cannot be taken away lightly. “The right to vote is a vital right. Your (ECI) exercise must be conducted with due diligence. Suppose a voter was lax and did not respond. Does that mean he forfeits his right forever? A voter may have been unable to respond for various reasons. His name is now missing from the draft roll. He approaches the authorities with his documents, but you insist that he submit Form 6... items.title: Move Supreme Court: Delhi High Court to advocate seeking ₹50 crore compensation from CJP for disruption
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday asked an advocate to approach the Supreme Court with his plea seeking directions to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to deposit ₹50 crore as interim compensation for the alleged inconvenience and disruption caused to residents of the national capital by its protests. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma noted that the Supreme Court is already seized of similar issues. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta also said that the apex court is dealing with similar matters. Therefore, the Court told the petitioner, advocate Rakesh Kumar Saini, that he should approach the top court. "The judicial discipline warrants that, in such an eventuality, this court must stay its hands away from the proceedings and should not pass conflicting orders," the High Court said in its order. It then disposed of the public interest litigation (PIL). Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Justice Sanjay Sharma Saini had filed a PIL in the High Court seeking directions to the Central government and other authorities to initiate proceedings against the CJP. He sought imposition of a collective or community fine and compensation for affected members of the public. He alleged that the CJP and its associates violated conditions imposed on protests at Jantar Mantar, resulting in traffic congestion, disruption of daily activities and inconvenience to traders, commuters, office-goers and schoolchildren. According to the petition, the party was initially permitted to hold a protest against alleged examination paper leaks and the Union Education Minister, but continued occupying the protest site beyond the permitted period. It further alleges that subsequent protest activities, including demonstrations seeking the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, caused disruption in central Delhi. The petition also sought the appointment of a high-powered committee to invite compensation claims from affected citizens and determine the amounts payable. Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma and Central Government Standing Counsel (CGSC) Premtosh Mishra appeared for the Central government.

items.title: RPNLU Prayagraj finance controller removed after refusing VC’s ₹70,000 academic incentive
items.summary: The finance controller (FC) of Dr Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLUP) was removed after he refused to approve a ₹70,000 academic incentive for the Vice-Chancellor (VC) Usha Tandon , a Dainik Bhaskar report has claimed. The report from September 8 claims that the University has replaced 9 FCs in the past two years. It further claims that the latest removal, that of Siddharth S Tripathi, followed his refusal to approve a ₹70,000 academic incentive to the VC. Tripathi reportedly claimed that the VC could not be entitled to this incentive. When contacted, Tripathi refused to comment on the matter. In a telephonic conversation with Bar & Bench, the University's public relations officer (PRO) Prakash Tripathi said that the power to remove or appoint the FC rests with the State government and not the VC. When asked whether the VC was drawing such an incentive and the basis for the same, the PRO last week requested for a query on email. A response to the same is awaited. The University has also been facing allegations of irregularities in its recent recruitment of 12 assistant professors. In a press note issued on August 20, it has denied the irregularities and mentioned having filed a police complaint against "defamatory" press coverage. Subsequently, the Uttar Pradesh government ordered a probe into the recruitment . More recently, on September 21, Justice Vinod Diwakar of the Allahabad High Court ordered a judicial probe into the allegations of caste-based harassment and discrimination by a faculty member at the University. Justice Vinod Diwakar However, a Division Bench of Justices Siddhartha Varma and Kunal Ravi Singh questioned the order and said that there was no occasion to order a judicial inquiry when an Equal Opportunity Cell is already in place at the University. An appeal against the order was placed before a bench headed by Chief Justice Arun Bhansali , who has recused himself from the matter. It is yet to be heard further. Note: An earlier copy of this report stated that as per the University Act, the Executive Council appoints the FC in consultation with the State government. The same was inaccurate as it holds true only for the appointment of the first FC. The error is regretted.

items.summary: A painting of Gandhi and Muhammad Ali Jinnah has become the centre of a communal controversy in Kerala. The artwork at Kashi Art Cafe in Fort Kochi was created by Malayali artist Riyas Komu in 2008. But a north Indian influencer questioned why the cafe displayed Jinnah’s portrait, served beef and was located in an area with a Muslim population. The controversy widened after influencer Diya Krishna commented “Sad reality” under the video and later defended herself by citing her Muslim friends and relatives. items.title: Theni jailbreak: Last 4 of escaped prisoners caught
items.summary: The last four of the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from the District Jail at Thekkampatti in Tamil Nadu's Theni district were taken into custody on Wednesday, October 28, with the last two accused surrendering. The latest two, identified as siblings Thirupathi and Meenatchi Sundaram, surrendered at the Kudalur police station while two other accused, Regin and Ponmuthuselvam, were arrested earlier in the day. The jailbreak took place late on Monday, October 26, when the prisoners allegedly attacked prison staff and fled the premises. According to the Prison Department, the incident occurred around 10 pm when some inmates raised an alarm, claiming that a prisoner in the third block was experiencing an epileptic seizure. When Grade II warden Stalin Prabhu, who was on duty in the block, entered to check on the prisoner, the inmates who were lodged in the same cell allegedly attacked him and attempted to escape. They then allegedly confronted guards, snatched the keys, and opened the main entrance to flee the prison. The jail, which has an authorised capacity of 200 inmates, housed 334 prisoners at the time of the incident, the Prison Department said. The escapees were from several districts, including Madurai, Ramanathapuram, Salem, and Villupuram, and had been lodged in the jail in connection with various criminal cases. Following the jailbreak, the Theni district police formed 17 special teams to trace the escapees. Nine prison staff members were suspended for dereliction of duty. A case was registered at Kandamanur police station under Sections 121(1) (voluntarily causing hurt), 296(b) (obscene acts in public), 118(1) (causing hurt by dangerous weapons), 309(4) (robbery), 109 (attempt to murder) and 262 (attempting to escape from lawful custody) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Five of the escapees were caught in the early hours of Tuesday, October 27, while eight others were apprehended that evening. The Prison Department has now reportedly urged the implementation of high-tower CCTV surveillance with armed personnel deployed across 125 prisons. Prison staff have also been instructed to use firearms if any inmates attempt to escape. The jailbreak triggered sharp criticism from opposition parties, who alleged failure of law and order in the state.

items.title: NDA sweeps Karnataka Council polls, wins all four seats in setback to Congress
items.summary: In a setback to the ruling Congress, the BJP-JD(S) alliance won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23, taking both teachers' and both graduates' constituencies. Congress had earlier held one of the four seats. The biggest upset for Congress came in the Bengaluru Teachers' constituency, where five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman Puttanna lost to NDA candidate AP Ranganath. In the North-East Teachers' constituency, BJP candidate Shashil G Namoshi secured his fifth victory, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur. In the West Graduates' constituency, SV Sankanur won his third consecutive term, defeating Congress' Mohan Limbikai. In the South East Graduates' constituency, BJP's KM Suresha defeated Congress candidate Shashi Hulikuntemutt. The results have rejuvenated the NDA partners, who were jolted earlier this year when 11 of its MLAs cross-voted in the June polls to seven Legislative Council seats. Congress won five of those seven seats, while the BJP won two. In May, Congress also retained the Davangere South and Bagalkot bypolls despite strong internal differences. The victory is being seen as the result of coordinated effort between the BJP and JD(S), which has shown that the partners can transfer their support to each other's candidates. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar acknowledged the defeat and said the party would introspect. He insisted, however, that the outcome was not a "precursor" to future elections, as the NDA partners have interpreted it. Although the Council results will not affect the stability of the Congress government, the NDA's strong performance is likely to give the opposition momentum.

items.title: Three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav found dead in Delhi
items.summary: Three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav, 42, was found dead near his SUV close to Maujpur metro station in northeast Delhi on Tuesday night, October 27. Delhi Police said the preliminary investigation suggests he may have died by suicide. The circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear, and a postmortem examination is underway at Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital as on Wednesday. According to the Indian Express, Yadav was found unconscious beside his black Scorpio-N by a female friend at around 9 pm. The two had travelled from Sonipat to Delhi earlier that day. A senior police officer said the woman had gone to Sonipat to meet Yadav and tell him that she could no longer remain in contact with him. Yadav subsequently dropped her off near Maujpur metro station. When he stopped responding to her calls, she went looking for him and found him lying beside his vehicle near Gate No. 1 of the metro station. She took him to a hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival. Around midnight, the Jafrabad police station received information from Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital that a man had been brought dead. Police identified him as Yadav, who lived primarily in Sonipat, Haryana, and ran an online sports academy called Anshneer Sports Academy. He is survived by his wife and their three-year-old daughter. Police have initiated proceedings under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Yadav, who hailed from Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh, was diagnosed with paralysis caused by polio as a child. He initially pursued wheelchair tennis before switching to para-athletics in 2013. He subsequently emerged as a prominent competitor in javelin throw, discus throw and shot put. He won gold in the men’s F55 javelin throw at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, setting an Asian record with a throw of 29.84 metres. At the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, he won gold medals in both javelin and discus throw, taking his tally to three titles at the continental competition. However, his career was disrupted by an anti-doping case. The National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) provisionally suspended him after a sample collected out of competition in Bengaluru in October 2023 tested positive for stanozolol, an anabolic steroid banned under anti-doping regulations. Yadav was consequently unable to compete at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games in Japan, held in October. items.title: ‘97 lakh voters deleted in TN’: Stalin urges President to intervene in SIR irregularities
items.summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin urged President Droupadi Murmu to initiate parliamentary action against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He also urged the President to seek the Supreme Court’s opinion on the deletion of 97,37,832 electors from Tamil Nadu’s voter lists. Stalin also called for the restoration of the pre-SIR electoral rolls, an independent forensic audit of the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) digital voter databases, and measures to restore public confidence in elections, including a return to paper ballots. In a memorandum dated October 26, Stalin requested the President to send a message to both Houses of Parliament under Article 86(2) of the Constitution (Right of President to address and send messages to Houses), seeking consideration of action against Gyanesh Kumar, and to refer questions concerning the validity of the voter deletions and the functioning of the Election Commission to the Supreme Court under Article 143 (Power of President to consult Supreme Court). The memorandum, submitted on behalf of the DMK, contains nine demands, including the cancellation of the SIR across all states, an independent audit of the ECI’s digital systems, the preservation of official records relating to the revision exercise, and the counting of 100% of Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) slips pending a shift to paper ballots. Stalin alleged that the SIR exercise had resulted in the exclusion of genuine voters and that the deletions had disproportionately affected constituencies where the DMK had a strong support base. He also accused Gyanesh Kumar of taking unilateral decisions in the name of the Election Commission, overriding the recorded objections of the other two Election Commissioners. “The right to vote is the foundation on which every other institution of our Republic rests,” Stalin wrote, arguing that Articles 326 (Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of states to be on the basis of adult suffrage) and 324 (Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission) of the Constitution. items.title: Andhra CEO says no independent deletions. TNM’s questions about transparency remain
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Refuting a data-driven report by TNM, Andhra Pradesh’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) has said that “no suo moto deletions were carried out independently by officers.” The statement, posted on the Andhra CEO’s official X account, responded to TNM’s findings that Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) were listed as objectors in consolidated Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of 20,959 electors’ names in just 12 days. A report by TNM published on October 14 analysed data published by the Election Commission of India (ECI) between September 29 and October 10, under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Andhra Pradesh. During this period, 40,006 electors were listed for deletion through Form 7 applications. Of these, 20,959, or 52.38%, had an ERO or AERO listed as the objector.
